candidate.derivedAnswer: A. The rational numbers form a proper subset of the real numbers.
candidate.answerReason: Every rational number is real, and irrational real numbers exist, so the inclusion is proper.

methods.label: Compare the number sets
methods.explanation: All rational numbers are real numbers, but the real numbers also include irrational numbers. Therefore, the set of rational numbers is a proper subset of the set of real numbers.
methods.levelReason: This uses familiar number-set inclusion and the definition of a proper subset.
